final.object: One persistent indexed set of six architectural drawing sheets carrying owned cabin material and explicit project-role records.

swap.reason: The story depends on Marta’s owned cabin work, workshop and timber-book influences, and specific technical contributions within practice projects.

backdrop.reason: The sheets arrange actual drawings, construction photographs and finished views into comparisons, giving their transformations an explanatory role preserved in static fallbacks.

depth.reason: The sequence develops from identity and spatial drawings through structure and construction detail to a completed record answering the opening question.

clipart.reason: The central sheets contain her actual work and contribution records rather than serving as a generic architectural emblem.

honesty.reason: The final plan respects practice ownership, partner concept authorship, Marta’s defined roles, modelled performance and unresolved reproduction permissions.

thirty_seconds.reason: The first screen supplies her name, current role, work focus, owned cabin proof and a contact shortcut without requiring animation or full scrolling.

plain_reader.reason: The opening question and introduction use accessible language while the drawing-set sequence and precise role descriptions remain credible to architects.

judgement.summary: The plan uses six persistent drawing sheets to connect Marta’s cabin, technical practice contributions and teaching through her own drawing-set order. Its greatest weakness is that the promised visual comparisons remain dependent on inspecting unavailable assets, so their explanatory strength is not yet demonstrated.
